title: c says /k/
parentNote: Today c says /k/. It is made right at the back of the mouth — the back of the tongue humps up, touches, and pops — which makes it the hardest sound so far to feel, because nothing you can see moves. Its twin is /g/, made in exactly the same spot with the voice switched on, so "cap" and "gap" are the pair worth practising; a hand on the throat settles it. The other usual slip is "cuh" instead of a clean /k/, which turns cat into "cuh-at". One thing to know for yourself rather than to teach: this same sound gets written another way later in the course, so if your child meets it in a book and asks, you can simply say that English has more than one letter for it. Every c in today's lesson says /k/.

activities.mouthCue: The back of your tongue lifts up and touches the roof at the very back, then pops. No buzz at all.
activities.prompt: This one happens right at the back of your mouth. Keep it short and quiet.
Same spot at the back for both. One buzzes and one is just a pop.
Three quick pops. Two are at the back and one is at the front.
Pop at the back, wide vowel, tap at the front.
Same start. This one ends with the tongue up and humming.
A cab is a taxi. Back pop, front pop.
Nearly cab, but the last pop has no buzz in it.
Two sounds at the front, squashed up together. Say them both: /k/, /lll/.
Four sounds. The hum in the middle is easy to lose.
A clam shuts itself up inside two shells.
Both start at the back of your mouth. Hand on your throat: which one buzzes?
All three start the same. Everything depends on the last sound.
One of these has a hum hiding after the first pop.
